title: ops-weekly-sprint-27-sampling-experimentation-and-dashboard-consolidation
body:
Weekly ops note (Sprint 27) — focus: controlled sampling pilot, dashboard consolidation, and cost telemetry sanity checks.

Meeting context:
- Weekly ops sync: 2026-03-12 10:00 PT (recording in Slack thread).
- Attendees: Priya, Luis, Alyssa, Tom, Marta + on-call rotation (Eran covering).
- Primary goals this week: run controlled sampling pilot on high-volume production routes, remove duplicated Grafana panels across infra and serving dashboards, and validate cost telemetry alerts after budget rollup.

Key observations / metrics snapshot (end of week):
- Production RPS served by inference proxies: 18.2k RPS (24h avg).
- Trace ingest rate into pipeline A: ~2.9M spans/day (10% down from last week after preliminary filter tweaks).
- Median per-span ingestion size: 540 bytes.
- 95th percentile end-to-end trace latency for API request traces: 420ms (improved from 470ms after batching changes).
- Daily trace storage spend estimate (projected): $1,250/day before pilot; expected to drop ~20–30% under pilot.

Controlled sampling pilot (adaptive tail-preserving sampling):
- Summary: We deployed an adaptive sampling agent to Canary cluster (zone us-west-2b) that reduces sampling rate for high-volume endpoints while preserving full sampling for error and latency outliers. The goal is to cut ingestion and storage cost while keeping signal for debugging regressions.
- Implementation notes: sampling implemented at the service shim (patch in PR 482). The algorithm weights recent error/latency features and uses reservoir sampling for traces over 1s latency.
- Target routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat/stream. Piloted window: 48 hours (2026-03-11 04:00 -> 2026-03-13 04:00).
- Observed impact during pilot: overall span count decreased ~26% in canary; error trace retention stayed >95% for errors; tail latency traces (>1s) retention 93%.
- Risks/notes: internal SDKs that rely on 100% prefix traces for some debugging tasks will need a fallback to full sampling when debug flag is set. We observed two incidents where a customer-side debug session expected full context and was missing earlier prefixes — mitigation: a short-lived header we added to force full sampling on a per-request basis.
- Action items from pilot:
  - Luis G to run a sweep of customer-facing SDKs to add a standardized sampling-control header (due 2026-03-19).
  - Priya to prepare a short runbook section describing how to escalate and temporarily disable adaptive sampling for live debugging (due 2026-03-15).
  - Alyssa to quantify projected monthly cost savings if pilot scales to 100% traffic and produce a graph for next week’s GTM sync (due 2026-03-20).

Dashboard consolidation work (Grafana / internal dashboards):
- Motivation: multiple teams maintaining near-duplicate panels for latency, queue depth, and model utilization. This is causing confusing signal and frequent divergence in runbooks.
- Tasks completed this sprint:
  - Merged serving-runtime latency panels into a single shared dashboard (dash ID 589).
  - Removed three legacy panels that were stale/duplicated (notes kept in dash-migration log).
  - Introduced a unified top-left panel with traffic breakdown by route + 95th latency to make SRE on-call faster to triage.
- Observability changes committed: small refactor in dashboards repo (PR 475), plus an on-call dashboard alias documented in Confluence.
- Feedback loop: Dev-ex team to run a 1-week dogfood period and report missing panels.
- Action items:
  - Tom B to follow up with deck owners (infra, serving-runtime, platform-eng) and lock down ownership for merged panels (due 2026-03-17).
  - Marta to add a lightweight migration checklist to the dashboards repo README (due 2026-03-16).

Cost telemetry and alerting check-ins:
- Background: Finance requested a clearer mapping between trace storage and inference units to forecast run-rate costs for Dedicated customers. We’ve been rolling up trace/storage costs into the cost center dashboard.
- This week: validated budget rollup for project "inference-prod" and exercised the slack budget-alert pipeline.
- Findings:
  - Budget alert worked end-to-end; channel msg contained expected card but link resolution to storage report was slow (10–15s). Root cause: pre-signed URL generation service under load.
  - A labeling mismatch meant some trace storage was attributed to a misc-cost bucket; fixed by tagging pipeline PR 480.
- Action items:
  - Alyssa to add a synthetic test that triggers the budget-alert pipeline every 6 hours to detect regressions (due 2026-03-18).
  - Priya and Finance (contact: Daniel Park) to confirm the monthly allocation model for next quarter (meeting scheduled 2026-03-16).

Runbook updates and on-call notes:
- Added a new troubleshooting subsection: "When sampling drops necessary prefixes" describing how to temporarily override sampling and capture full traces.
- Clarified steps for "trace backlog" incidents (thresholds, alert routing to obs-oncall).
- Observability on-call rotation: Eran (primary) / Tom (secondary) for the week of 2026-03-15.

Open blockers and questions:
- Need product confirmation on whether debug sessions should default to force-full-sampled traces (product-ops preference currently unknown). Ticket JIRA-OBS-3268 opened.
- Potential compatibility issues with third-party tracing libs in older customer runtimes (tech debt). Luis to inventory by next week.
- Some dashboards still render slowly for >1000 series; investigate if Prometheus remote-write or Grafana-series-limit tuning helps. Ticket JIRA-OBS-3238 assigned to Marta.

Decisions made:
- Proceed to scale adaptive sampling to 50% of traffic for next sprint (canary -> staged rollout) conditioned on no regression in error-trace retention (threshold: >90%).
- Consolidated dashboards will be the canonical source of truth; teams must open a migration PR and link runbook ownership before removing old panels.

Next steps (next sprint):
- Expand sampling pilot to 50% traffic in staged rollout; monitor key metrics and rollback criteria (Priya/Luis, start 2026-03-17).
- Finish dashboard ownership handoffs and run the dev-ex dogfood (Tom/Marta, complete by 2026-03-19).
- Implement synthetic budget-alert test and validate end-to-end (Alyssa, 2026-03-18).
- Finalize runbook wording for sampling debug override and publish to Confluence (Priya, 2026-03-15).

Notes to reviewer:
- This doc is intentionally informal; it captures operational context and actionables for sprint-27. Please comment inline or add short calls-to-action in the Slack thread if you need deeper dives.
- I attached the key PRs and Jira IDs above; grab logs from the canary cluster if you want raw spans (canary cluster path: s3://obs-canary-spans/2026-03-11_to_03-13).

Signed-off-by: Priya Nair (obs lead)
